recreation_prompt_markdown:
# Recreation Prompt

Recreate a browser-native mobile portrait parkour platformer titled **Caped Rizz Runner**. Preserve a 3D-projected canvas traversal loop: left-side drag joystick controls momentum, right-side tap jumps only when grounded, gravity pulls the player down, rectangular roof platforms catch the player, falling below the world causes failure, and reaching a green finish roof wins the level. Levels become longer over time and become harder after level 5 through larger gaps, narrower platforms, and more lateral offset.

Build the public surface as a single self-contained `index.html` with inline CSS and JavaScript. The authored world is a satirical caped vigilante rooftop sprint with synthwave neon, anime/comic energy, meme feedback, and mobile-readable HUD. The avatar should have a recognizable mask-and-cape silhouette. The background should be a procedural neon skyline with a parody signal, moon, speed lines, and glowing rooftop grid. Use concise mobile copy: Start Parkour, Rooftop, EZ CLAP, sweaty mode, RIZZ LOST, Retry Run.
blueprint_markdown:
# Blueprint

## Source truth
The preserved source is a mobile-first 3D-ish canvas platform runner. The player controls a single avatar with a left-side drag joystick for horizontal/forward movement and a right-side tap for jump. Gravity, friction, max speed, rectangular platform collision, fall death at y > 600, finish-platform victory, level restart, and next-level progression are the protected mechanics.

## Remixed target
Caped Rizz Runner reframes the same traversal as a satirical neon rooftop parkour game inspired by caped vigilante tropes without using protected names. The focal actor is a tiny cape-wearing night runner crossing meme-branded rooftops toward an EZ CLAP finish tag.

## Protected mechanics
- Split touch model: left 60% drag joystick, right 40% tap jump.
- Physics constants: gravity, jump force, friction, max speed, momentum-based gaps.
- Platform generation semantics: safe starting roof, normal generated roofs, green finish roof.
- Collision/fall/win state flow and restart/next-level behavior.
- Level escalation after level 5 through larger gaps, narrower platforms, and wider x offsets.

## Transformable surfaces
HUD vocabulary, title, panels, background, avatar rendering, platform style, particles, audio mapping, meme feedback, progression copy, and visual palette are safe presentation surfaces.
